units.title: Paper 1 History and Culture of Bangladesh

topics.title: Topic 1 The struggle for control of the Indian subcontinent, 1204-1784

outcomes.text: Explain how the Turkish conquest happened under Bakhtiyar Khilji and the Sultans.
Describe the achievements of Bakhtiyar Khilji.
Explain the role of Sufis and Sufism in religious and political life.
Describe the achievements of the Ilyas Shahi, Hussain Shahi and Nusrat Shah dynasties.
Explain the diplomatic successes of Nusrat Shah and Akbar.
Assess the impact of Muslim rule on Bengal as a centre of culture, industry and trade.
Explain how Babur established the Mughal Empire in 1526.
Describe the First Battle of Panipath, the fighting methods used and why Babur won.
Describe Humayun's military, administrative and social achievements.
Describe Akbar's military, religious and administrative achievements.
Describe Jahangir's achievements and the growth of trade with the English.
Describe Shah Jahan's architecture, famine relief and military achievements.
Describe Aurangzeb's achievements and the role of the Subadars in Bengal.
Explain why the Mughal Empire grew weak.
Explain Aurangzeb's role in the Empire's downfall.
Explain the establishment, purpose and growth of the East India Company.
Explain the causes, events and impact of the Battles of Plassey and Buxar and land annexations.
Describe the roles of the Diwans and Nawabs in Bengal.
Explain the causes and organisation of Dual Administration.
Explain its economic and social effects.
Explain why Direct Rule was imposed through the 1784 India Act.
Describe how Direct Rule worked, what it introduced and its effects.
Describe the organisation of society in Bengal.
Describe early customs: religion, food, dress and the role of women.
Describe entertainment, village work (farming, cottage industry, commerce) and transport.
Give an overview of changes in music, dance, architecture and literature.
Explain what changed and what stayed the same in Bengal between 1204 and 1784.

topics.title: Topic 2 The years of growing opposition, 1784-1911

outcomes.text: Explain the political, military, economic and religious causes of resistance to the British.
Describe the Fakir and Sannyasi Movement, Titumir, the Indigo Revolt and the Faraizi Movement.
Describe the Bengal renaissance thinkers Rammohun Roy and Derozio and the education reformers Mohsin, Abdul Latif and Ameer Ali.
Explain how these thinkers developed nationalism and the wish for independence.
Explain the political, economic, military and religious causes of the Independence Struggle, including the Doctrine of Lapse.
Describe key events: Mangal Pandey and the Meerut sepoys, Bahadur Shah, the British retaking Delhi, Lakshmibai and Tatya Tope at Jhansi.
Explain why the Struggle failed: poor coordination and British military strength.
Describe the changes in rule set out in the Proclamation of Allahabad in 1858.
Describe British reprisals and Muslim distrust of the British.
Describe the impact on the Hindu community.
Describe Sir Syed Ahmad Khan's work promoting change.
Describe Hindu-Muslim and Hindu-British relations by 1905.
Explain the reactions to and effects of the 1905 Partition, including the Simla Deputation and the Muslim League.
Explain the causes and forms of opposition to the Partition.
Explain the reversal of the Partition in 1911 and its impact.
Describe how political and economic change affected farming, industry, trade, transport, communication and commerce.
Give an overview of changes in music, dance, architecture and literature.
Explain what changed and what stayed the same between 1784 and 1911.
Describe the reform offers: the 1909 Morley-Minto Reforms, 1919 Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, 1927 Simon Commission and 1935 Government of India Act.
Explain why the offers were rejected: the Rowlatt Act, the Amritsar Massacre, the Nehru Report and Jinnah's 14 Points.
Describe the 1940 Lahore Resolution and the 1946 Delhi Proposals.
Explain the causes and methods of opposition to the British in 1908-c.1930.
Describe the impact of the Armed Movement in Bengal.
Explain the 1916 Lucknow Pact and the roles of Tilak and Jinnah.
Describe the Non-Cooperation Movement and the 1923 Bengal Pact.
Explain the Cripps Mission of 1942 and the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
Describe the attempts to form a united Bengal in 1947.
Explain the 3rd June Plan and the Radcliffe Award and how British rule ended.
Compare East and West Pakistan in customs, culture and geography.
Describe the social, economic and political difficulties of establishing Pakistan's government.
Explain the growing differences between the two wings of Pakistan.
Compare rural and urban life.
Explain the language differences and the Urdu proposal.
Explain how government policies harmed East Pakistan's economy.
Explain East Pakistan's under-representation in defence and the differences in social welfare.
Explain the causes, actions and impact of the Language Movement.
Describe the causes, demands and impact of the Six Points of 1966.
Explain the Agartala Conspiracy Case and the central government's reaction.
Describe the mass uprising of 1969.
Describe Operation Searchlight and the events of the War of Liberation.
Explain why East Pakistan won independence.
Explain the cyclone's economic and political impact on East Pakistan.
Describe international support and the central government's response.
Explain the impact on the January 1971 election results.
Describe life and work in towns and villages in Bengal.
Give an overview of changes in music, dance, architecture and literature.
Explain what changed and what stayed the same between 1911 and 1971.
Explain the causes and effects of the 1971 parliamentary system, the 1973 election and the 1974 constitutional amendments.
Describe Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's presidency and his assassination in 1975.
Describe the political achievements of 1971-5.
Describe Bangladesh's condition in 1971 after the war and the Bhola cyclone.
Explain responses to hunger, housing, law and order and medical shortages.
Assess programmes for agriculture, industry and national unity, and the First Five-Year Plan.
Describe the role of literature and the arts in reconstruction and the social and economic achievements to 1975.
Describe the establishment of military rule.
Describe Ziaur Rahman's presidency, the BNP and the 1977 Martial Law Decree.
Assess policies on irrigation, food, free markets, press freedom and education.
Summarise the social, political and economic achievements of 1975-82.
Explain the causes and effects of the 1982 military coup.
Assess Ershad's administrative and constitutional reform.
Assess economic reform: irrigation, education, the 1983 Development Programme, privatisation, foreign investment, land reform and decentralisation.
Explain why and how the 1982-90 government ended and summarise its achievements.
Explain why and how government changed in 1991 and the return to parliamentary democracy.
Describe Khaleda Zia's premiership and why a female prime minister mattered.
Assess social achievements: free primary education and compulsory education for girls to tenth grade.
Assess political achievements: elected mayors and two-tier local government.
Assess economic achievements: banking controls, trade agreements and inward investment.
Assess international relations: visits to China and India and UN peacekeeping.
Explain why and how government changed in 1996 and describe Sheikh Hasina's premiership.
Describe progress towards food self-sufficiency.
Describe economic developments: telecom and digital industries, electricity privatisation, remittances.
Assess international relations, including water and trade treaties with India.
Explain what changed and what stayed the same between 1971 and 2001.
Describe present-day religious and cultural festivals and the rural past in cultural dance.
Describe the work of literary figures: Tagore, Kazi Nazrul Islam and Begum Rokeya.
Describe art such as Zainul Abedin's showing social and political struggles.
Describe monuments and memorial days: the National Monument, Shaheed Minar and International Mother Language Day.
Explain the commemoration of the Bangla language and the strength of support for the new Bangladesh.

units.title: Paper 2 Environment and Development of Bangladesh

topics.title: Theme 1 Environment and natural resources > Topic 1 Landscape

outcomes.text: Name and locate the major hills (Chattogram Hills, Madhupur Tract, Borendra Tract, Tippera Surface) and describe how they look.
Describe the flood plains, deltas and coastal plains of Bangladesh.
Name and locate the main rivers: Jamuna, Brahmaputra, Padma, Meghna, Surma, Tista and Karnaphuli.
Explain how and why river flow changes after rain, using a hydrograph.
Explain seasonal changes in river flow.
Describe river erosion, transport and deposition.
Describe the characteristics and formation of Bangladesh's flood plains and deltas.
Describe the structure of the Earth: crust, mantle, outer and inner core.
Name the major tectonic plates of Southeast Asia.
Explain how plate movement causes earthquakes and the Himalayas and Chattogram Hills.
Explain the causes, effects and responses to river bank erosion.
Explain the causes, effects and responses to river floods.
Study a river flood case study: year, causes, impact on people and economy, responses.
Explain the causes, effects and responses to earthquakes in Bangladesh.
Study an earthquake case study: why Bangladesh is prone, past events, damage, ways to reduce impact.

topics.title: Theme 1 Environment and natural resources > Topic 2 Weather and climate

outcomes.text: Explain the link between pressure and the south-west and north-east monsoons.
Explain the reasons for a tropical climate's high annual temperature.
Describe monthly temperature and rainfall variation in Bangladesh.
Explain the global temperature increase and its reasons.
Explain the effects on Bangladesh: sea level rise and more weather hazards.
Explain mitigation and adaptation strategies used in Bangladesh.
Explain the causes of cyclones and drought.
Study a cyclone case study: year, flooding, impact on people and economy, responses.
Study a north-west Bangladesh drought case study: what drought is, why the area is at risk, effects on people and crops, actions to reduce impact.

topics.title: Theme 1 Environment and natural resources > Topic 3 Natural resources

outcomes.text: Describe the location and characteristics of hill forests and the Sundarbans mangroves.
Explain the value of forests for soil, coast protection and biodiversity.
Describe economic exploitation of forests for timber, pulp and paper.
Explain the impact of deforestation and sustainable forest management.
Describe inland (including aquaculture) and marine fishing.
Explain the fishing industry's contribution to the economy.
Explain the causes and consequences of overfishing and sustainable management.
Describe the water sources (rainfall, rivers, groundwater) and their advantages and disadvantages.
Describe supply methods such as dams, wells, tube wells and desalination.
Explain arsenic risks from groundwater overuse.
Explain sustainable water management as the economy grows.
Distinguish renewable from non-renewable energy.
Describe the location and use of coal, oil and natural gas.
Explain how electricity generation causes pollution.
Describe the location and generation of hydro-electric power.
Explain the development of affordable and clean energy in Bangladesh.
Study a renewable energy case study: location, funding, how it works, contribution, advantages and disadvantages.

topics.title: Theme 2 Economy and production > Topic 4 Economic development

outcomes.text: Define the primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary sectors.
Describe how each sector's contribution has changed since 1971.
Define GDP and describe how Bangladesh's GDP has changed since 1971.
Compare Bangladesh's economic growth with other countries.
Describe changes in the pattern and volume of international trade in raw materials, food and manufactured goods.

topics.title: Theme 2 Economy and production > Topic 5 Agriculture and its importance to Bangladesh

outcomes.text: Distinguish food crops from cash crops.
Describe changes in rice, wheat and pulses production since 1971.
Describe changes in sugar cane, tea and jute production since 1971.
Distinguish physical factors (relief, climate, soil) from economic factors (demand, labour, technology, capital, land fragmentation, chemicals, seeds, irrigation, aid).
Explain how these factors affect the location and development of one food crop and one cash crop.
Study one food crop and one cash crop: location, physical needs, economic factors, methods, trends.
Describe aquaculture development and its environmental effects.
Explain how overuse of land causes soil erosion.
Explain the causes and effects of salinisation.
Study an irrigation project case study.
Explain the development of sustainable agriculture.
Define food security.
Explain the factors influencing food security.
Explain the contribution of cereals, pulses and animals, including fish.
Explain how Bangladesh can end hunger, achieve food security and improve nutrition.

topics.title: Theme 2 Economy and production > Topic 6 Manufacturing industry

outcomes.text: Explain the conditions for manufacturing growth: raw materials, education, capital, infrastructure, ICT, transport and globalisation.
Explain how conditions affect cottage industry, garments and textiles, and capital-intensive industries.
Study a ready-made garment manufacturer case study.
Describe working conditions in some factories and their effects on workers.
Explain the importance of factory regulation for decent work.
Explain how manufacturing causes pollution.
Explain actions that make manufacturing more sustainable.

topics.title: Theme 2 Economy and production > Topic 7 The service sector

outcomes.text: Distinguish the formal from the informal sector.
Explain the advantages and disadvantages for informal workers.
Explain why moving people from the informal to the formal sector is difficult.
Explain the sector's role in enabling investment and mobilising savings.
Explain the role of microcredit in empowering women.
Explain how hi-tech knowledge and research will help the economy.
Compare water, road and rail transport for freight and passengers.
Explain the challenges of improving transport.
Describe strategies for safe, affordable and sustainable transport.
Explain the impact of urban transport on air quality and strategies to reduce it.

topics.title: Theme 3 Population and society > Topic 8 Population structure, growth and impact on quality of life

outcomes.text: Interpret the changing population pyramid of Bangladesh.
Explain how births, deaths, infant mortality, dependency ratios and life expectancy change population.
Interpret birth and death rate graphs and population data.
Calculate natural increase or decrease.
Define literacy, numeracy, life expectancy and per capita income.
Describe how each indicator has changed since 1971 across Bangladesh.
Compare Bangladesh with other countries using data.

topics.title: Theme 3 Population and society > Topic 9 Migration and urban growth

outcomes.text: Describe types of migration: internal, international, voluntary and forced.
Explain rural push factors and urban pull factors.
Explain reasons for migration into and out of Bangladesh, including refugees.
Describe the impact on rural areas.
Explain the challenges and benefits of refugee migration.
Study the growth of Dhaka: water, power, traffic, pollution, employment and housing.

topics.title: Theme 3 Population and society > Topic 10 Health and education

outcomes.text: Describe the roles of government, private and NGO health care providers.
Explain the importance of disease control programmes.
Explain health care as a way to improve quality of life, and the improvements still needed.
Study a health care programme case study.
Explain access and equality in education between genders and between rural and urban areas.
Describe progress in literacy, numeracy and standards.
Explain the role of education in gender equality and empowering women and girls.
Explain the need for occupational and professional skills.
Describe educational programmes and improvements needed.
Study an educational programme case study.

topics.title: Theme 4 Sustainable development > Topic 11 Sustainable Development Goals

outcomes.text: Explain the meaning and importance of sustainable development.
Explain that action in one area affects others and development must balance social, economic and environmental sustainability.
Assess how successful Bangladesh has been towards the SDGs.
Describe the role of the United Nations in helping Bangladesh achieve the SDGs.
